title: HubSpot static auth access token: relation to the legacy private app token and to Service Keys
summary: A static auth access token of a project-based app next to the legacy private app access token and the Service Key, which share the Bearer header.
rationale: Claim pages-do-not-relate-static-auth-and-private-app-tokens (class unresolved) records that neither the authentication overview nor the legacy private apps page mentions the other credential or states a shared format. Whether static auth tokens are a separate role from Service Keys and from legacy private app tokens is not settled (open question static-auth-vs-service-key), and rotation and expiry are not stated (static-auth-rotation-and-expiry). The pat- lead on the private app contract is not extended to this role (static-auth-lexical-shape-unstated). A claim of equivalence either way would be invented. Contract claims cited: static-auth-access-token/pages-do-not-relate-static-auth-and-private-app-tokens, static-auth-access-token/bearer-carrier-shared-by-oauth-static-and-private-app-tokens.

expectation.rationale: No outcome is asserted. Settled by: a HubSpot statement relating static auth tokens to legacy private app tokens and Service Keys.

sources.supports: If you want to limit distribution of your app to a single authorized account, you'll use a static auth access token.
Private apps allow you to use HubSpot's APIs to access specific data from your HubSpot account. ... which will generate an access token that's unique to your app.
An example request is provided below using a placeholder static auth access token.
